# Voice & Tone

Use to establish or preserve the writer's character, adapt tone, learn from samples, or choose expressive techniques. [Language & Style](language-and-style.md) handles wording and sentence correctness; this reference covers character and effect.

## Distinguish voice, tone, register, and style

| Decision | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Voice | Recognizable character expressed through perspective, diction, rhythm, imagery, and relationship with readers |
| Tone | Attitude toward the subject, reader, or situation in this passage |
| Register | Language associated with a setting, activity, relationship, or community, including vocabulary, grammar, and formality |
| Writing style | Project conventions or a broader set of expressive choices; establish which meaning applies |

A brand may keep a recognizable voice while changing tone. An author, narrator, character, or contributor can legitimately use different voices across works. Formality is one choice, not a measure of quality. Here, voice means authorial character; active/passive grammar belongs in Language & Style.

## Choose the intended voice

Identify whose voice the text represents. Use the brief, applicable project guidance, and relevant samples. Distinguish the agent's replies from the voice requested for the text.

Interpret vague requests as observable choices. "More professional" may mean more precise, restrained, courteous, or formally structured. Use the context to select an interpretation; ask when alternatives would substantially change the result. A short edit does not need a persona document or brand questionnaire.

Prefer samples from a comparable genre and relationship. A formal policy provides limited evidence for a condolence note. If the user requests a new direction, adapt supported features rather than treating past style as binding. Clarify consequential conflicts between the brief and examples.

## Adapt writing samples

Look for repeated choices in point of view, address, formality, terms, rhythm, imagery, emotion, directness, and humour. Distinguish stable patterns from topic-specific choices or errors. One unusual phrase does not define a voice.

Convert observations into decisions for the new work. "Expert but approachable" might require precise terms explained where necessary and direct claims with appropriate limits. "Measured and personal" might require restrained evaluation and first-person observations, but does not authorize an invented biography or anecdote.

Adapt useful patterns without copying distinctive passages or importing the sample's facts, promises, emotions, or experiences. Treat style inferred from a short or mismatched sample as provisional. Do not require a large sample collection for every edit or claim exact reconstruction from limited evidence.

## Adapt tone to the situation

Consider the event, stakes, communication stage, relationship, and known circumstances. A meaningful achievement may suit celebration; a consequential failure may require restraint, responsibility, and a useful next step. Familiarity, warmth, seriousness, and formality can vary independently.

Natural writing need not be informal; professional writing need not be cold. Preserve a suitable brand or author direction.

Respond to stated emotion and known circumstances. An export failure establishes inconvenience to address, not proof that every reader is distressed. Do not tell an unknown reader how they feel or promise a recovery time that is unavailable.

Separate acknowledgment from factual agreement. Recognize a concern without endorsing an unsupported premise. Explain a consequential disagreement with evidence and a useful next step; do not add praise to soften every correction or manufacture an opposing position to sound balanced. Retain justified agreement, courtesy, and requested advocacy.

If an export failed and retry is available, "The export failed. Please try again" states the known result and action. "A tiny hiccup; we'll fix it in no time" minimizes the problem and invents a promise. The right amount of detail depends on the actual failure and next step.

## Use emotion and humour deliberately

Show care through accurate acknowledgment, useful help, respect for the reader's time, and clear responsibility. Apologize when the speaker's role and facts warrant it; do not invent blame, intimacy, or a personal bond. Preserve sincere acknowledgment when removing it would change the intended relationship.

Judge emotional intensity by purpose. A personal letter, advocacy piece, eulogy, poem, or fictional scene can legitimately be affectionate, angry, exuberant, or unsettling. Do not automatically convert it to restrained business writing.

Use humour for an identifiable effect, such as rapport, satire, or a distinctive perspective. Check who or what it targets, its cultural assumptions, whether it works across intended settings, and whether it obscures important instructions. Optional humour with uncertain fit can be omitted without removing warmth. Preserve requested satire or dark humour unless a concrete problem warrants revision.

## Use comparisons and emphasis

Choose a comparison, metaphor, repetition, question, or other device for what it helps readers understand, notice, feel, or judge. Keep deliberate expression that serves the brief. Use literal wording in instructions and professional explanations when figurative language would obscure the meaning.

For an explanatory analogy, check which relationship it clarifies and where the comparison stops. Remove or replace it if it implies an unsupported mechanism or needs more explanation than a direct account. An analogy can explain a claim; it cannot establish that the claim is true.

In routine professional writing, avoid stock "not X, but Y" and "not only X but also Y" reframing and self-answered questions. State the positive claim directly. Use a contrast or question when it resolves a real misunderstanding, explains an actual distinction, or serves the requested style. Do not invent an opposing view merely to reject it, or imply a range or consensus the material does not support. Keep meaningful repetition or a three-item list; do not invent another point for symmetry.

Make persuasive emphasis accurate. An opportunity, cost, or risk can be foregrounded, but retain qualifications that change the decision. Do not manufacture urgency, credentials, testimonials, shared values, or lived experience. Check consequential factual claims with [Content & Evidence](content-and-evidence.md).

Retain supported conviction and intended enthusiasm; remove intensity that exceeds the evidence or situation. Neutral wording is not automatically more accurate.

## Preserve voice and cultural meaning

Before revising, identify the perspective, cadence, imagery, stance, or deliberate irregularity that must remain. Repair a local problem locally when sufficient. Compare the revision with its surroundings and relevant samples. Consistency permits a coherent range, distinct characters, and individual contributors.

Check that corrections preserve the requested identity. A grammatically correct rewrite can still erase the writer's character. Watch for generic assistant phrasing replacing a restrained author, promotional excitement replacing a factual update, or identical reassuring language across different situations. A particular word alone does not establish poor quality.

Interpret address, indirectness, humour, and self-presentation in the relevant language and setting. Do not infer individual preferences from nationality or impose one culture's business style. When adapting across languages, preserve the intended relationship and effect; use [Multilingual Writing](multilingual-writing.md) for fidelity and locale decisions. Seek qualified feedback when a consequential nuance cannot be resolved.

Preserve character while adapting tone. Fix demonstrated mismatches; for a review, explain the intended effect, problem, and suitable change. Label preferences as preferences. Offer alternatives for meaningful choices, and stop when further rewrites add no benefit.
